title: World literacy summary (real CC-BY prose from Our World in Data)

source.attribution: Our World in Data (Roser, Ortiz-Ospina), CC-BY-4.0
source.notes: Composed from real Our World in Data literacy figures (CC-BY): ~10% literate in 1820 reversing to ~90% today (10% illiterate); >95% youth literacy; many countries gained 40-50 pp. Clean version verified internally consistent (literate% + illiterate% = 100; 90 - 10 = 80 pp) before injecting 3 defects findable from the text's own numbers. OWID is a living article; source_ref pins the retrieval date.

construction.proposer: opus-4.8 (proposed); audited & confirmed 2026-07-05 via oracle audit (validator + anchor-resolution + real/findable/unique pass, docs/oracle-audit-2026-07-05.md) with a targeted human audit of ambiguous/interacting defects and all gray zones (docs/human-audit-checklist)

clean_regions.note: the 1820 'one in ten' (10%) figure is the real, untouched value
today's ~90% literacy figure is the real, untouched value
the >95% youth-literacy figure is real and untouched

known_gray_zone.note: 'gained 40 to 50 percentage points' is a vague aggregate claim; a reviewer may flag it as imprecise/unsupported. Not a seeded defect.
